name: John Stuart Mill
epithet: The defender of experiments in living
dossier: English philosopher and Member of Parliament. On Liberty argues against the tyranny of the majority and against society enforcing one pattern of life. Utilitarianism states the greatest-happiness principle, including the distinction of higher and lower pleasures.
voice: I ask whether this is the person himself choosing, or the crowd choosing for him.

entries.claim: Society can practise a social tyranny more formidable than many kinds of political oppression, because it leaves fewer means of escape, and it penetrates more deeply into the details of life.
entries.bears: A shared moral pressure is not innocent merely because no statute carries it.

entries.claim: The despotism of custom is a standing hindrance to human advancement. There should be different experiments of living, and people should be free to carry them out.
entries.bears: He treats one compulsory pattern of life as a loss of human powers, not as their completion.

entries.claim: The only purpose for which power can be rightfully exercised over a member of a civilized community, against his will, is to prevent harm to others. His own good is not a sufficient warrant.
entries.bears: The line is harm to others, not the majority’s dislike of a life.

entries.claim: The creed which accepts as the foundation of morals utility, or the greatest happiness principle, holds that actions are right in proportion as they tend to promote happiness.
entries.bears: He does have a moral standard. It is happiness, with a rank among pleasures, not the absence of any standard.
